headline_notes: Amber — statutory expenditure. Charged on the Consolidated Fund by law and not put to a vote: debt servicing, and the salaries and pensions the Constitution protects. It runs A$4.7m to A$17.5m across the series, between 3% and 6% of the total.
Grey — the Development Fund line inside each total. Head 02, Local Contribution to the Development Fund (LCDF). Not additional to the total; a component of it.
Why statutory has to be separate

Total operating budget = appropriation + statutory. It is the total operating budget, not the appropriation, that equals the "original budget" column in the Annual Account — so any reconciliation to the accounts that uses the appropriation alone will be short by the statutory amount.

The same split runs through supplementaries. The 2017 Supplementary Budget No.1 moves A$8,569,194: A$7,539,240 appropriated in the Act, A$1,029,954 statutory, printed separately in the volume. Where a supplementary volume is held, both parts are shown; where only the Act survives, the Appropriated column is filled and Statutory is blank because the Act does not state it.
Appropriation quadruples 2011–2026, A$84m to A$408m. The Development Fund line grows twenty-fold, A$7.5m to A$148m — from 9% of the appropriation to 36%.
Supplementary appropriation reaches 14.8% of appropriation in 2018 and 24.8% in 2019, and 96% of the 2019 total went to the Development Fund rather than to any ministry.
2020 is not comparable: the volume was retabled in the third quarter and appropriates February to December only.
2019 has no outturn row — the Annual Account 2019 is held but has no usable text layer.

Supplementary Acts are not held for 2001, 2002 or 2005. ⚠️ Corrected 2026-08-28 (b10): this line formerly read "…2001, 2002, 2005, 2013 or after 2019". Three supplementary Acts for service year 2013 are held (Nos. 1, 2 and 3 of 2013, A$6,616,643 together), as are the 2021 and 2022 Acts — the Reconciliation sheet of this same workbook already used the 2021 and 2022 ones. A blank means no instrument in the archive, never that none was passed. PacLII's Kiribati sessional series stops at 2022, so 2023–2026 are untested rather than empty.
Twenty-seven of the 69 Acts are image-only scans read by OCR, tier C.

2026-08-28 (worker b10, tension T39) — the 1994 and 1995 supplementary cells. 1994 was A$2,383,083 and is now A$3,013,084; 1995 was A$630,000 and is now A$2,381,488. The A$630,000 is Supplementary Appropriation Act 1995 (No. 4 of 1995), which is short-titled 1995 and appropriates for service year 1994 — deemed to commence 1 November 1994, its memorandum naming November and December 1994. It was filed on its title year against this workbook's own rule that service year is the only safe key, and the two Acts that do serve 1995 (No. 9 of 1995, A$1,440,788; No. 2 of 1996, A$940,700) were absent altogether. Every figure is read on two independent copies, PacLII and parliament.gov.ki. See the cell comments on F8 and F9, and the Tensions Register entry T39.

2026-08-28 — a self-contradiction inside this workbook, recorded and NOT yet resolved. The "In 2025 prices" sheet carries a supplementary figure for 2013, 2021, 2022 and 2025 where this sheet is blank, and a 2016 figure of A$26.1m against this sheet's A$2.4m. Deflated back by that sheet's own index, its column F reproduces the full statutory total for 2013 (A$6,616,643), 2016 (A$26,097,364), 2018, 2019, 2021 (A$25,463,614) and 2022 (A$11,909,085). The real-terms sheet is therefore the complete series and this nominal sheet is the incomplete one. Only the 1994 and 1995 cells are corrected above, because those are the ones the evidence was worked through end to end; the rest is filed at tension T45 and is owed a decision, not a quiet edit.

reconciliation_notes: 2023 closes with no supplementary appropriation at all — the finding for that year, and it now survives an explicit challenge. But it was NOT a quiet year: A$11,559,233 was spent on Debt Servicing outside the appropriation, and the Annual Account books it as un-authorised.

The 2024 recurrent budget volume's Table 5(b) states a 2023 revised budget A$11,588,977 higher (A$329,721,435). The head-by-head diff (2026-08-28) localises 99.74% of it to ONE head, Debt Servicing: the volume revises it 4,055,383 -> 15,639,616 where the account revises it 4,055,383 -> 4,080,383. All 23 departmental heads and the LCDF agree to the dollar in both.

The item is the Government's payment of a guaranteed Kiribati Provident Fund loan to Air Kiribati Limited for twin otter aircraft, A$11,584,233 — Annual Account 2023 p.31 NOTE 5, 'Statement of Un-authorized Expenditure', and NOTE 4 Contingent Liabilities; 2024 Recurrent Budget Appendix 5(A)/(B) pp.115-116 ('a special one-off payment'); Fiscal Strategy 2024 p.14. Expenditure in EXCESS of the appropriation, not an addition to it — so no supplementary.

CORRECTED 2026-08-28 (C-2026-08-28-12). The superseded wording of the cell above read: "2023 closes with no supplementary at all, which is the finding for that year: there was essentially none." It is corroborated on its literal terms and retired only for its gloss: 'essentially none' reads as nothing material having happened, and A$11.56m outside the appropriation is material. Kept here rather than overwritten.
Only 2024 (1.56%, A$6.3m) and 2025 (1.56%, A$6.3m) remain open. PacLII's Kiribati sessional legislation stops at 2022, so no instrument exists to test them against yet.

The 2021 chain is built from two Acts on PacLII and gives a revised budget of A$304,889,602. The 2022 recurrent budget volume, an entirely separate document, prints 2021 revised expenditure as A$304,889,601. One dollar apart.

The Appropriation Acts for 2020, 2021 and 2023, and the supplementary Acts for 2013, 2014, 2016, 2019, 2021 and 2022, are not on parliament.gov.ki at all. They were already in this hub, in L0 — Evidence / PacLII — Kiribati Law / legis / num_act, which holds 123 appropriation instruments running from 1979 to 2022. Ninety-four carry full text in the HTML; the rest are PDFs alongside it, some of them scans needing OCR.

Note the naming again: the Act that appropriates for service year 2021 is titled "Appropriation Act (No.2) 2020", and the one for 2023 is "Appropriation Act 2022". Service year, not title year, is the only safe key.
